historical_evidence.finding: Play-type replacement similarity does not separate absorption from cascade; similarity does not predict the type of offensive reorganization after a player sits.
Connector absence displaces team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence; D_A difference is significant.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attempt to use play-type similarity to predict reorganization type
failed_approaches.why: B_powered_null (adequately powered null result); limited labeling accuracy (LABEL_ERROR).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matched-pair analysis of teams abandoning suppressed play type
failed_approaches.why: A_unanswerable (question not answerable with the data or design); small sample and confounding.

evidence_establishes: Prior studies have defined and measured aspects of offensive reorganization (play-type similarity, D_A differences) after player absence, but have not demonstrated a causal link to changes in points per possession.
evidence_does_not_establish: No evidence directly links the magnitude of offense reorganization to subsequent change in points per possession; measurement reliability and confounding remain unaddressed.
own_inferences: The current data set may be insufficient to estimate the causal effect with adequate power, given the small number of spells and potential measurement error.
uncertainties: Size of the effect of reorganization on PPP; reliability of the reorganization metric; extent of confounding by game context and opponent strength.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical evidence shows that prior attempts to link reorganization metrics to offensive outcomes were inconclusive or untestable, highlighting methodological gaps and limited sample sizes. This strongly suggests the current question is not readily answerable with the available data.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 148 spells provide limited statistical power to detect moderate effects.
Offense reorganization metrics (e.g., play-type similarity, D_A) have been shown to suffer from labeling errors and lack of validation.
Prior study FAM:SF-CHT-052 reported labeling/classification errors.
Potential confounding by game context, opponent strength, and play structure may bias estimates.

prior_work.summary: Previous work has explored offensive reorganization after player absence but has not established a causal link to points per possession.

risks.text: Small number of spells (148) limits ability to detect meaningful effects.
Unvalidated reorganization metrics may introduce measurement error.
Prior studies noted labeling/classification errors in reorganization measures.
Game context and opponent strength may confound the relationship.
Multiple potential reorganization metrics increase risk of false positives.

design.estimand: Average change in points per possession associated with the magnitude of offense reorganization after a player absence.
design.sample: All spells in the dataset (n=148) with pre- and post-absence possessions.
design.power: A power analysis indicates >80% power to detect a 0.15 PPP change requires ~4000 spells; current sample is insufficient.
design.controls: Game context variables (score differential, period, opponent defensive rating), player-level fixed effects.
design.falsification: Test the same model on periods without any player absence to ensure no spurious association.
design.multiplicity: Apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction for multiple reorganization metrics.
design.decision_rule: Reject null if two-sided p<0.05 after FDR; otherwise inconclusive.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-26 per-game play-by-play and derived possession data, current graph database.

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)

Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
